58236.name: Film Analysis
58236.entryRequirements: Positive BSA Media and Culture / Media en Cultuur or for switchers to Media and Culture: positive BSA Media and Information.
58236.recommendedPriorKnowledge: (EN) Analysis skills attained in Media Aesthetics and/or a good familiarity with the basic terminology and analysis skills used in film and television analysis, based on, for example, the book Looking at Movies (Barsam/Monahan) or Film Art: An Introduction (Bordwell/Thompson). For the video-essay, some basic knowledge of video editing software is also highly recommended. (NL) Analyseskills opgedaan bij Media Aesthetics en/of de basis terminologie en analyseskills uit de film- of televisieanalyse, bijvoorbeeld aan de hand van het boek Looking at Movies (Barsam / Monahan) of Film Art - An Introduction (Bordwell / Thompson). Voor het video-essay is enige kennis van 'editing software' ook sterk aangeraden.

61667.name: Philosophy of the Humanities 2: (Media and Culture)
61667.entryRequirements: Positive BSA in Media and Culture or for switchers from M&I to M&C: a positive BSA in Media and Information
61667.recommendedPriorKnowledge: This course presupposes a comprehensive understanding of the materials used in the previous course, Philosophy of the Humanities 1 (Media Studies). It is recommended to first follow Philosophy of the Humanities 1 before enrolling in Philosophy of the Humanities 2. It is recommended to keep the texts used in the previous course as background material for this course. Exchange students: The readings of Philosophy of the Humanities 1 will be made available on Canvas for exchange students who want to follow Philosophy of the Humanities 2, and it is recommended they familiarise themselves with these readings.

sourceUse: The exact-target official public page lists Film Studies before Television and Cross-Media Culture. The dated 39570 guide confirms three separate 12 EC choice groups in year two, with named film and television units in each, and a 24 EC common year-two sequence. The Film example illustrates one Film course per group and does not suggest that mixing is prohibited. The English page and dated table agree on 60 credits in each year. The guide uses the title Media Culture in Transformation.

progression.yearOne: Living Information, Media Aesthetics, Media Culture in Transformation and Doing Media Studies 1 lead into Media Theory, Media Research, Current Themes and Doing Media Studies 2. Media Research applies first-term media foundations and includes writing. Literacy, tutoring and academic writing carry zero additional credits.
progression.yearTwo: Film Practices in blocks 1–2, Film Analysis in 2–3 and Advanced Topics: Film in 5–6 make up the three 12 EC choices. Positive binding study advice governs access. Media Aesthetics prepares for Practices and Analysis, and Media Aesthetics, Media Theory and Media Research prepare for Advanced Topics. Philosophy 1 in block 4 precedes Philosophy 2 in block 5. Global Media Culture and Media Worlds complete the common 24 EC.
progression.yearThree: The ordinary example uses the second-semester 18 EC seminar and thesis. Course 58087 is offered in either semester and must be completed within one. Its entry condition requires all first-year and mandatory second-year courses except the selected production course. That exemption is for thesis access, so Film Practices remains in the degree.
progression.openChoice: 42 EC remain open under the dated electives guidance. A minor, electives, approved external study or placement can contribute. Off-institution study needs Examination Board permission, and introductory electives usually have a 12 EC cap with stated minor and language exceptions.
